issue: Author is matched with instr(author, ?), which is case-sensitive, not with LIKE ? ESCAPE '\' as the spec requires on both columns. Author search breaks AC2 and AC3.
evidence: `WHERE title LIKE ? ESCAPE '\\' OR instr(author, ?) > 0`. The seed author is 'Martin Fowler', so q=fowler (the AC2 example) and q=FOWLER both miss 'Refactoring'. Only q=Fowler matches.

issue: Off-by-one in the length limit. A query of exactly 100 characters after trim is rejected, but AC6 says 100 → 200 and only 101 → 400.
evidence: `if (q.length >= MAX_QUERY_LENGTH)` with MAX_QUERY_LENGTH = 100, so q='a'×100 returns 400.

issue: q is not type-checked. A repeated or object q is coerced with String() and searched, not rejected with 400 'Query must be a single string'.
evidence: `const q = String(req.query.q ?? '').trim();`. ?q=a&q=b gives the array ['a','b'], which becomes 'a,b' and returns 200. ?q[x]=1 becomes '[object Object]'.

issue: `_` is not escaped, so it still works as a single-character LIKE wildcard on title. This breaks AC8.
evidence: `query.replace(/\\/g, '\\\\').replace(/%/g, '\\%')` has no `_` replacement. q=_ becomes pattern '%_%', which matches every title, but the expected result is [].
